tagline: Up the Mohawk beside the canal that went around its falls.
intro: Out of Waterford the byway follows the Mohawk west on county roads and the old Riverview Road, crossing the river at Aqueduct and ending 26 miles on in Schenectady. At the Waterford end the five locks of the Waterford Flight, finished in 1915, lift boats 169 feet from the Hudson to the Mohawk in a mile and a half.

The first Erie Canal made much the same climb at Cohoes on sixteen locks, and getting through them took a whole day. In 1831 a railroad was laid between Albany and Schenectady chiefly so travelers could skip them.

moments.title: Cohoes Falls
moments.text: The Mohawk goes over a ledge some 1,000 feet wide and up to 90 feet high, except in dry summers, when the canal locks and the power turbines take all of it.

moments.title: Rexford
moments.text: From the Route 146 bridge you can still see the arches of the 1841 aqueduct that carried the canal and its towpath across the Mohawk.

moments.title: Stockade District
moments.text: Dutch traders put up twelve houses inside a wooden stockade here in 1661. The neighborhood has been lived in ever since and keeps more than 40 houses past their 200th year.
